nodes.name: Ni(OH)2 Hydrothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: Subsequently, above cleaning NF was immerged into 30 mL DI water solution containing 2 mmol Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, 10 mmol urea, and 4 mmol NH4F. After stirring for 10 min, the mixed solution was put into a Teflon-lined stainless steel autoclave, which was then maintained at 120 °C for 6 h. After the temperature was naturally cooled down, the green Ni(OH)2 precursor was rinsed with DI water and dried at 60 °C.

nodes.name: Ni3S2 Sulfurization
nodes.procedure: A piece of the as-prepared Ni(OH)2 precursor was put into 30 mL DI water solution containing 10 mmol Na2S·9H2O. After stirring for 20 min, the mixed solution was put into a Teflon-lined stainless steel autoclave, which was then maintained at 120 °C for 2 h. After the temperature was naturally cooled down, the black Ni3S2 catalyst was rinsed with DI water and kept in DI water to avoid oxidation.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni₃S₂ nanosheets retain the vertical self-supported nanosheet structure with thickness of tens of nanometers after sulfurization from Ni(OH)₂ precursor.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphology of different samples was characterized by scanning electron microscopy (SEM). ... the structure of Ni₃S₂ nanosheets have no obvious change compared to the Ni(OH)₂ precursor.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows Ni₃S₂ nanosheets with lattice fringes of 0.286 nm, 0.237 nm, and 0.166 nm corresponding to (110), (111), and (-121) planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution TEM image displays lattice fringe spacings of 0.286 nm, 0.237 nm and 0.166 nm very close to the (110), (111) and (-121) planes of Ni₃S₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping confirms uniform distribution of Ni and S throughout Ni₃S₂ nanosheets with atomic ratio Ni:S of 6.5:3.5.
nodes.evidence_snippet: elemental mapping images displayed in Fig. 1f show that the two existing elements are Ni and S, which are uniformly distributed throughout inside the nanosheet. The atomic ratio of Ni:S is measured to be 6.5:3.5.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms complete phase transformation from Ni(OH)₂ (PDF #40-0215) to Ni₃S₂ (PDF #73-0698) after sulfurization.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) characterization was employed to identify the phase of Ni(OH)₂ and Ni₃S₂. ... the peaks of the Ni(OH)₂ phase have completely disappeared and transferred into the Ni₃S₂ phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms Ni₃S₂ phase with Ni 2p peaks at 855.6 eV (Ni 2p₃/₂), 873.3 eV (Ni 2p₁/₂) for oxidized Ni-S species and 852.6 eV for Ni-S bonds; S 2p peaks at 168.1 eV (S-O), 162.1 eV (S-S), 163.2 eV (Ni-S). Negative binding energy shift indicates lower Ni valence state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As for the Ni 2p spectrum of Ni₃S₂ (Fig. 2c), two fitted peaks located at binding energies of 855.6 and 873.3 eV accompanied by two satellite peaks are respectively assigned to Ni 2p₃/₂ and Ni 2p₁/₂ related to the surface oxidation of nickel sulfides. ... the characteristic peak located at the binding energy of 852.6 eV belongs to Ni–S bonds. ... the S 2p XPS spectrum exhibits peaks locked at binding energies of 168.1 and 162.1 eV ... and the peak locked at the binding energy of 163.2 eV fits well with the metal–sulfur bonds of Ni–S species.

properties.description: Blue-tinted silicon wafer placed on white paper
Electrolyte solution used in electrochemical measurement

nodes.characterization_summary: CV in non-faradaic region gives double layer capacitance Cdl = 9.07 mF cm⁻² for Ni₃S₂ (vs 6.74 mF cm⁻² for Ni(OH)₂), corresponding to higher ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the Cdl value of the Ni₃S₂ catalyst is 9.07 mF cm⁻², which is 1.35 times larger than that of Ni(OH)₂ (6.74 mF cm⁻²), indicating that the Ni₃S₂ catalyst possesses enhanced intrinsic activity.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows charge-transfer resistance Rct of Ni₃S₂ is 0.35 Ω, much lower than Ni(OH)₂ (4.37 Ω).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Nyquist plots ... illustrate that the Ni₃S₂ catalyst possesses a smaller charge-transfer resistance (Rct) value of 0.35 Ω than that of Ni(OH)₂ (4.37 Ω).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM confirms Ni₃S₂ lattice fringes of 0.286 nm (110), 0.237 nm (111), 0.166 nm (-121).
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution TEM image displays lattice fringe spacings of 0.286 nm, 0.237 nm and 0.166 nm very close to the (110), (111) and (-121) planes of Ni₃S₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern shows diffraction rings confirming polycrystalline Ni₃S₂ phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Diffraction rings of Ni₃S₂ in the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern further verified the successful synthesis of Ni₃S₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: Contact angle test shows excellent hydrophilicity of Ni₃S₂ catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The contact angle test displays that a drop of electrolyte fleetly sticks to the surface of Ni₃S₂, indicating the Ni₃S₂ catalyst possesses excellent hydrophilicity.
